summary.whatChanges: The prettyJSON middleware now parses a clone of the response body inside a try/catch, passing the response through untouched when the body is empty, not valid JSON, or already consumed. When it does prettify, it deletes the now-stale Content-Length header. Tests cover these cases.
behaviorChanges: 204/304 and empty JSON-typed responses pass through instead of erroring when pretty printing is active
Responses with a JSON content-type but non-JSON body are returned unchanged, with original headers (ETag, Content-Length, custom) intact
A response whose body was already read by another middleware no longer causes a failure; it is left as is
Prettified responses no longer carry a stale Content-Length header
The original response body is no longer consumed by the middleware (a clone is read instead)
risks: Cloning the response buffers the body an extra time, adding memory/CPU overhead for large JSON payloads and potentially affecting streamed responses
Removing Content-Length changes response framing (clients/proxies may see chunked instead of fixed-length responses)
The broad catch silently swallows all parse and clone errors, hiding genuine malformed-JSON problems
